title: eval-harness: add prompt-regression CI hook and quality gating for prompt sets
author: Priya Sharma
description: Context: We need automated detection of prompt-set regressions in PRs that touch model-serving configs, prompt templates, or downstream scoring code. This PR adds a CI hook to run the eval-harness against a curated set of prompt-sets and gating rules to prevent quality regressions from reaching main. Motivation: avoid silent regressions in prompt-output quality caused by model pinning, tokenization, or subtle runtime changes. What this PR does: (1) adds a new eval-harness CI job (ci/workflows/eval-harness-prompt-regression.yml) that runs the prompt-regression runner on changed prompt-sets and model-related code; (2) implements a lightweight prompt-regression runner (eval-harness/ci/prompt_regression_hook.py) that loads changed prompt-sets, runs a small fixed sample through the eval harness and compares metrics against a golden baseline stored in eval-harness/ci/baselines/*.json; (3) introduces gating rules (eval-harness/config/quality_gates.yaml) where teams can declare thresholds (delta on BLEU/ROUGE/QA-F1/semantic-similarity) and severity (warn/block); (4) docs and onboarding guide (docs/ops/eval-gating.md) describing how to add prompt-sets and opt into relaxed gating. Rollout plan: start as opt-in on the eval-harness repo, then enable as required for PRs touching redwood/core-serving and docs after a 2-week opt-in window. Checklist: - [x] CI workflow that runs only on relevant file changes and on a schedule - [x] baseline storage and update command (eval-harness/ci/update_baseline.py) - [x] gating config format and parsing library - [x] docs and engineer-facing onboarding - [x] unit tests for the runner and gating logic (tests/ci/test_prompt_regression.py) Usage notes: The job runs in a dedicated CI container that caches model artifacts. When a gate is violated with severity=block the job exits non-zero and posts a summary to the PR checks pane including the offending prompt examples and metric deltas. Engineering notes: - Baselines are intentionally small (few-shot) to keep CI runtime <10m. - The runner supports a --golden-commit override to re-evaluate baselines for baseline refresh PRs. Related: ENG-4821, QA-197. See docs/ops/eval-gating.md for operator instructions.
commits: feat(eval-harness): add prompt-regression runner and baseline format
ci: add eval-harness-prompt-regression workflow and caching
docs: add eval-gating onboarding and update baseline guide
test: add unit tests for gating logic and runner edge cases

release_notes:
- Add prompt-regression CI hook for eval-harness with configurable quality gates and baselines.
- New docs to onboard teams to quality gating and baseline updates.
- Opt-in rollout; will be enforced for redwood/core-serving after 2-week opt-in.
additional_notes: CI history: initial run failed due to cache misconfiguration and a flaky test (tests/ci/test_prompt_regression.py::test_timeout). Fixed by reducing baseline sample size and increasing test timeout. The gating thresholds are conservative and can be tuned per-team via eval-harness/config/quality_gates.yaml. This PR is intentionally self-contained and MVP-focused: it provides a clear path to expand metric integrations (embedding-similarity, human-benchmark hooks) in follow-up PRs.
